json.text:
NordCare Pflegekasse   |   Long-Term Care Claims Operations   |   Fictitious insurer — demonstration use only
Bremen, 24 September 2026
Your Long-Term Care Application: What Happens Next

Dear Mrs. Hoffmann,
Thank you for submitting your application for long-term care benefits (case reference NC-2026-081345). We are glad to support you through this process, and this letter explains what will happen between now and your care-level decision.
The Steps Ahead
The Medical Service (Medizinischer Dienst, MD) will carry out an independent assessment of your care needs.
The MD will contact you directly to arrange a convenient time for this assessment, either at home or, if you are currently hospitalized, at your place of care.
As soon as the assessment is complete, we will inform you of the outcome without delay.
How the Assessment Works
A trained assessor from the Medical Service will visit you to understand exactly what kind of support you need day to day. During this visit, the assessor will look at:
Which care level (Pflegegrad) best reflects your current situation
What kind of support would help stabilize or improve things
How much care and assistance you are likely to need, and in what form
It genuinely helps if the person who supports you day to day is present for this conversation, so please feel free to have a family member or your representative join you.
Please let us know if your situation changes.
If you need to be admitted to hospital while your application is being processed, please tell us as soon as possible so we can coordinate the next steps for your assessment with the Medical Service accordingly.

How Long This Will Take
From the date we received your application, we have 25 working days to reach a decision if you are being cared for at home. This is the standard timeframe that applies to most applications like yours.
If we are unable to meet this deadline for reasons within our control, we will pay you €70 for every week the decision is delayed, until the decision is issued. This does not apply if the delay is caused by something outside our control, such as waiting for information we have requested from you.
We're Here to Help
Our care advisory team is available if you have questions about your entitlements or the process itself. They can talk you through your options, help you understand your personal care plan once it is available, and make sure you know what support is available to you at every stage.
If anything about this letter is unclear, or if your circumstances change in the meantime, please get in touch using the contact details below — quoting your case reference NC-2026-081345 helps us assist you faster.

Kind regards,
NordCare Pflegekasse — Long-Term Care Claims Operations

json.name: Case_Handover__Ownership_Protocol_NordCare_Pflegekasse___illustrative.txt
json.text:
Case Handover & Ownership Protocol
Controlled transfer of a case between Input & Output Management, the Case Handler, the Medical Service, and the Decision Intelligence Agent — NordCare Pflegekasse, Long-Term Care Claims Operations
1. Purpose
This protocol defines how ownership of a long-term care case is transferred in a controlled, traceable manner between the functions and agents involved in processing an application, from intake through to decision and, where applicable, objection handling. It ensures that at every point in the process exactly one party is accountable for the case.
2. Scope
Applies to every application for determination or change of long-term care need (Pflegebedürftigkeit) handled by NordCare Pflegekasse, from receipt of the Antrag to case closure.
Covers handovers between Input & Output Management, the Case Handler, the Medical Service (MD), the Decision Intelligence Agent, and, where an objection is raised, the objection-handling function.
Does not cover the Medical Service's own internal assessment workflow, which is a third-party activity outside NordCare's operational control.
3. Ownership Model
Input & Output Management owns the case from receipt of the application until the Case Handler has created the case record and confirmed applicant identification.
The Case Handler (Sachspezialist für Pflege) owns the case from case creation through deadline-type determination, confirmation letter dispatch, information gathering, and completeness checking, up to transmission of the assessment order.
Ownership passes to the Medical Service (MD) for the duration of the assessment; NordCare retains monitoring responsibility but not operational control during this period.
The Case Handler resumes ownership on return of the assessment report (Gutachten) and assignment of the Gutachten to the case.
The Decision Intelligence Agent holds working ownership of the plausibility check and draft benefit-entitlement determination, under the Case Handler's supervision, until the benefit decision is documented.
The Case Handler owns issuance, dispatch, and archiving of the care decision notice (Pflegebescheid).
Where an objection (Widerspruch) is submitted, ownership passes to the objection-handling function on receipt and triage of the objection.
4. When a Handover Is Required
The case moves from intake (Input & Output Management) to case handling (Case Handler).
The assessment order is transmitted to the Medical Service.
The Gutachten is returned by the Medical Service and assigned to the case.
The Decision Intelligence Agent's plausibility check and draft decision are handed to the Case Handler for review and finalization.
The benefit decision is documented and the care decision notice is generated, sent, and archived, closing the case.
An objection is received and the case is triaged to the objection-handling function.
5. Mandatory Handover Package
Case reference and applicant identification
Current process stage and status (e.g., awaiting MD assessment, Gutachten received, decision drafted)
Actions completed to date, with dates and the responsible party for each
Open items and any outstanding requests (e.g., a missing-information request still awaiting a response)
Applicable due date (deadline type and current pause/resume status, per the Deadline & Escalation Procedure)
Named sending owner and named receiving owner, both explicitly acknowledging the transfer
6. Handover Procedure
The sending owner assembles the mandatory handover package described in Section 5 and attaches it to the case record.
The sending owner confirms the case is in a consistent state (no unresolved data conflicts, all completed actions logged) before initiating the handover.
The receiving owner reviews the handover package and either accepts ownership or returns the case with a documented reason if the package is incomplete.
On acceptance, the case management system timestamps the change of ownership and records both the sending and receiving owner.
Where the Decision Intelligence Agent is the receiving party, its output remains subject to Case Handler review before any decision is finalized; agent output is never transmitted to the applicant unattended.
The sending owner remains available to answer clarifying questions for a reasonable period after handover, particularly where the Medical Service or the applicant requests clarification on information supplied before the handover.
7. Ownership During Repeat Assessments and Objections
Where a repeat assessment (Wiederholungsbegutachtung) is triggered, the Case Handler who owned the original case retains ownership of the new assessment cycle where practicable, to preserve continuity of case knowledge; a formal handover under Section 6 still applies if the case is reassigned to a different Case Handler. Where an objection is received, ownership passes to the objection-handling function, but the original Case Handler's case history, the Gutachten, and the documented benefit decision must be included in full in the handover package, since the objection review depends on this record.
8. Closure Criteria
The care decision notice has been sent and archived, or the objection process (if any) has reached a final outcome.
All handovers relevant to the case are logged with sending owner, receiving owner, and timestamp.
No open items remain unresolved at the point of closure.
The complete case record, including the Gutachten and the documented benefit decision, is retained per NordCare's records-retention rules.
9. Roles
Input & Output Management: scans, classifies, and triages incoming documents; owns the case until initial case creation.
Case Handler (Sachspezialist für Pflege): primary case owner across most of the process; accepts and initiates handovers; makes final decisions on agent-drafted output.
Zero-Gap Agent: supports the Case Handler during the information-gathering and completeness-check stages; not itself a case owner.
Decision Intelligence Agent: checks the plausibility of the Gutachten and drafts the benefit-entitlement determination for Case Handler review; holds working, not final, ownership.
Team Lead: resolves disputed or rejected handovers between functions.
Process Owner: monitors handover completeness and timeliness across the end-to-end process.
10. Legal & Regulatory References
§ 18 Abs. 1 SGB XI — the insurer must commission the Medical Service within 3 working days of application receipt, which sets the latest point by which the Case Handler must have completed the intake-to-case-handling handover.
§ 18 Abs. 4 SGB XI — the insurer must supply the Medical Service with the documents necessary for the assessment; the handover package to the Medical Service stage must reflect this obligation.
§ 18c Abs. 2 SGB XI — the care decision notice must present and explain the Gutachten result transparently; the handover from the Decision Intelligence Agent to the Case Handler must preserve the information needed to meet this requirement.
Illustrative / fictitious document prepared for internal demonstration purposes. NordCare Pflegekasse is a fictitious insurer. Not an approved operational policy.

json.name: Completeness_Check_Work_Instruction_NordCare_Pflegekasse___illustrative.txt
json.text:
Completeness Check & Missing-Information Work Instruction
Verifying mandatory order information before commissioning the Medical Service (MD) — NordCare Pflegekasse, Long-Term Care Claims Operations
1. Purpose
This work instruction defines how case handlers and the Zero-Gap completeness-check capability verify that an incoming long-term care application contains the mandatory order information required to commission the Medical Service (Medizinischer Dienst, MD) with the determination of care need. It applies from case creation up to transmission of the assessment order.
2. Scope
Applies to all applications for initial determination or change of long-term care need (Pflegebedürftigkeit) received by NordCare Pflegekasse.
Covers process steps: gather case-specific information, check completeness of mandatory order information, request missing information where required, and generate/transmit the assessment order.
Does not cover the Medical Service's own assessment process, which is a third-party activity outside NordCare's operational control.
3. Mandatory Order Information (Stammdaten)
The Medical Service Bund (MD-Bund) assessment guidelines specify the minimum data set an insurer must hold before it may commission an assessment. The fields below reflect that mandatory set as currently implemented in NordCare's intake process.
Data field
Description
Source
Insurer / care fund reference
NordCare Pflegekasse case-handling entity and member number under which the application is registered.
Applicant record
Applicant identification
Full name, date of birth, sex, and current address of the person for whom care need is being assessed.
Antrag form
Application reference number
Unique case ID assigned at intake; used to link all subsequent correspondence and the assessment order.
Case system
Date of application receipt
Calendar date the application was logged as received; anchors both the 3-working-day commissioning clock and the applicable decision clock.
Case system
Applicant contact details
Telephone and/or email/postal address for the applicant or their authorized representative, for confirmation and follow-up correspondence.
Antrag / Fragebogen
Authorized representative details (if applicable)
Name and proof of authority (Vollmacht) where the application is filed by a legal guardian or appointed representative.
Supporting document
Requested assessment type
Initial classification, change/re-assessment (Höherstufung), or repeat assessment (Wiederholungsbegutachtung).
Antrag form
Deadline-type indicator
Flag for expedited handling: hospital/inpatient rehabilitation (5 working days) or home care with announced Pflegezeit (10 working days), otherwise standard (25 working days).
Fristtyp determination
Consent / data-sharing acknowledgement
Confirmation that the applicant has been informed of data transfer to the Medical Service for assessment purposes.
Antrag form
This checklist is illustrative and reproduces the category structure of the MD-Bund mandatory data set (Antragsinformationen / Stammdaten, Anlage 1 to the Begutachtungs-Richtlinien). It must be validated against the current published Anlage 1 before any operational use.
4. Completeness Check Procedure
Retrieve the case file created at intake and confirm the applicant has been identified without ambiguity (no unresolved duplicate or conflicting case).
Compare the case file against the mandatory order information checklist in Section 3, field by field.
Where the Zero-Gap Agent performs the check, review its completeness result and confidence flags before relying on them for a missing-information decision.
If every mandatory field is present and consistent, mark the case ready for order transmission and proceed to Section 6 of the Deadline & Escalation Procedure.
If any mandatory field is missing, unreadable, or contradictory (e.g., mismatched applicant name between the application and an identity document), mark the case incomplete and proceed to Section 5.
Record the completeness outcome, the fields checked, and the reviewer or agent identifier in the case log.
5. Missing-Information Handling
Prepare a missing-information request (Aufforderung) listing precisely which mandatory fields or documents are outstanding.
Route the request for human review before dispatch; the Zero-Gap Agent drafts the communication but does not send it unattended.
Send the request to the applicant or their authorized representative without delay. The statutory decision clock is paused from the day this request is received by the applicant, not from the day the gap was identified — do not delay dispatch once the gap is confirmed.
Log the dispatch date in the case file; this date starts the pause of the applicable decision deadline.
On receipt of the completed information, re-run the completeness check (Section 4) before resuming case handling.
If the applicant does not respond within the locally agreed follow-up window, refer to the Deadline & Escalation Procedure for the applicable escalation trigger.
6. Roles
Case Handler (Sachspezialist für Pflege): owns the case, makes the final completeness determination, and approves outgoing correspondence.
Zero-Gap Agent: performs the automated completeness check against Section 3, flags missing or inconsistent fields, and drafts the missing-information request for human review.
Input & Output Management: scans, classifies, and triages incoming documents and resubmissions, and dispatches approved correspondence.
Team Lead: reviews cases where the Zero-Gap Agent's confidence flag is low or where the applicant has not responded to a request.
7. Escalation
Escalate to the Team Lead when: the Zero-Gap Agent cannot reach a confident completeness determination; the applicant disputes a missing-information request; or a repeat request is required for the same case. See the Deadline & Escalation Procedure for time-based escalation triggers.
8. Closure Criteria
All mandatory order information fields are present, consistent, and evidenced in the case file.
The completeness outcome and reviewer/agent identifier are logged.
Where a missing-information request was issued, the pause start and resume dates are recorded.
The case is handed to the assessment-order generation step only after these criteria are met.
9. Legal & Regulatory References
§ 18 Abs. 1 SGB XI — insurer must commission the Medical Service within 3 working days of application receipt; MD-Bund defines the mandatory document set for commissioning.
§ 18 Abs. 4 SGB XI — obligation to provide the Medical Service with documents required for the assessment itself (separate from the commissioning data set above).
§ 18c Abs. 6 SGB XI — the decision deadline is paused from the day the applicant receives a request for still-missing mandatory documents, and resumes on receipt.
MD-Bund Begutachtungs-Richtlinien, Ziff. 3.1 and Anlage 1 — defines the Antragsinformationen / Stammdaten mandatory for commissioning.
Illustrative / fictitious document prepared for internal demonstration purposes. NordCare Pflegekasse is a fictitious insurer. Not an approved operational policy.

json.name: Deadline_Escalation_Procedure_NordCare_Pflegekasse___illustrative.txt
json.text:
Deadline & Escalation Procedure
Managing the statutory commissioning and decision clocks for long-term care applications — NordCare Pflegekasse, Long-Term Care Claims Operations
1. Purpose
This procedure defines how NordCare Pflegekasse determines, tracks, pauses, and escalates the statutory deadlines that apply to long-term care applications, from application receipt through to the written care-level decision.
2. Scope
Applies to every application for determination or change of long-term care need from the point of receipt to dispatch of the written decision (Bescheid).
Covers deadline-type determination, the 3-working-day Medical Service commissioning window, pause/resume handling, and escalation when a deadline is at risk or missed.
3. Deadline Types (Fristtyp)
Deadline type
Trigger condition
Legal basis
5 working days
Applicant is currently in hospital or an inpatient rehabilitation facility.
§ 18a Abs. 5 SGB XI — assessment must be completed by the 5th working day after application receipt.
10 working days
Applicant is in a home environment (not receiving palliative care) and caregiver leave (Pflegezeit / Familienpflegezeit) has been announced or agreed with the employer.
§ 18a Abs. 6 SGB XI — assessment must be completed within 10 working days of application receipt.
25 working days (standard)
All other cases; the default deadline type unless an expedited trigger applies.
§ 18c Abs. 1 Satz 1 SGB XI — standard written decision deadline.
Deadline type is determined at intake based on the applicant's situation as stated in the application; it does not depend on whether the order information is complete.
4. Clock Start, Pause, and Resume Rules
Both the 3-working-day commissioning clock and the applicable decision clock (5 / 10 / 25 working days) start on the date the application is received, regardless of completeness.
The insurer must commission the Medical Service within 3 working days of receipt using a secure electronic channel, based on the mandatory order information available at that point (see the Completeness Check & Missing-Information Work Instruction).
If mandatory order information is missing, the decision clock is paused only from the day the applicant receives the missing-information request — not from the day the gap was identified, and not automatically.
If the request is delayed after the gap is confirmed, the days between confirmation and dispatch still count against the decision deadline.
The decision clock resumes on the day the requested information is received back at NordCare Pflegekasse.
Log clock-start, pause-start, pause-end, and clock-resume dates in the case file for every application.
5. Escalation Triggers and Levels
Level
Trigger
Action / owner
Level 1 — Case Handler
Case approaching 70% of the applicable decision deadline with no missing-information request yet issued.
Case Handler reviews and either progresses the case or issues a missing-information request without delay.
Level 2 — Team Lead
Mandatory 3-working-day commissioning window is at risk, or applicant has not responded to a missing-information request within the locally agreed follow-up period.
Team Lead reviews case status, confirms whether a further request or direct outreach is warranted, and reassigns capacity if needed.
Level 3 — Process Owner
Standard 25-working-day (or shortened) decision deadline has been missed, triggering the statutory penalty; or a recurring pattern of missed deadlines is identified.
Process Owner logs the penalty trigger, confirms root cause, and reports the case in the governance review.
6. Escalation Record — Minimum Data
Case reference and applicant identification
Deadline type and applicable decision date
Date of application receipt, and pause/resume dates if applicable
Current process step and case handler
Reason for escalation and requested action
Named receiving owner and next review date
7. Penalty and Compliance Consequences
If NordCare Pflegekasse fails to issue its written decision within the applicable deadline, it must pay the applicant €70 for every started week the deadline is exceeded, continuing until the decision is issued. This penalty does not apply where the delay is not attributable to NordCare Pflegekasse, in which case the deadline is paused until the delay is resolved.
Legal basis: § 18c Abs. 5 SGB XI.
8. Roles
Case Handler: monitors deadline status for assigned cases and triggers Level 1 escalation.
Zero-Gap Agent: surfaces cases approaching a deadline threshold and flags whether a missing-information request is outstanding.
Team Lead: owns Level 2 escalations and follow-up on non-responsive applicants.
Process Owner: owns Level 3 escalations, penalty tracking, and periodic governance review.
9. Governance
The Process Owner reviews deadline performance monthly, including cases approaching or exceeding statutory deadlines, penalty payments triggered, and recurring root causes (e.g., systematic delay in issuing missing-information requests).
10. Legal & Regulatory References
§ 33 Abs. 1 SGB XI — benefits and the decision process begin upon application (Antragsprinzip).
§ 18a Abs. 5 und 6 SGB XI — 5- and 10-working-day expedited assessment deadlines.
§ 18 Abs. 1 SGB XI — 3-working-day Medical Service commissioning deadline.
§ 18c Abs. 1 SGB XI — standard 25-working-day written decision deadline.
§ 18c Abs. 5 SGB XI — €70-per-week penalty for missed decision deadlines and conditions for non-attributable delay.
§ 18c Abs. 6 SGB XI — pause and resume mechanism for missing mandatory documents.
§ 37 SGB X — rules on notification/delivery (Bekanntgabe) of written or electronic decisions.

Operational Governance & Control Policy
Management controls for ownership, deadlines, escalations, and continuous improvement across the Zero-Gap process — NordCare Pflegekasse, Long-Term Care Claims Operations
1. Purpose
This policy defines the management controls that govern the end-to-end long-term care application process at NordCare Pflegekasse, covering ownership, deadline compliance, escalation handling, and continuous improvement across the completeness-check, deadline-management, case-handover, and objection-handling procedures.
2. Governance Objectives
Ensure clear, single-point accountability for every case at every process stage.
Maintain compliance with statutory commissioning and decision deadlines.
Detect and escalate at-risk or non-compliant cases before statutory consequences are triggered.
Provide management visibility into process performance through a consistent, agreed KPI set.
Drive continuous improvement by identifying and addressing recurring root causes of delay or rework.
3. Proposed KPI Set
KPI
Definition
Target / illustrative threshold
% applications with complete order info on first check
Share of applications where the Zero-Gap Agent's first completeness check finds all mandatory order information present, with no missing-information request required.
Illustrative: 85%
Average time to issue missing-information request
Average elapsed time from confirmed identification of a completeness gap to dispatch of the missing-information request to the applicant.
Illustrative: 1 working day
% assessment orders transmitted within 3 working days
Share of cases where the assessment order is transmitted to the Medical Service within the statutory 3-working-day commissioning window.
Illustrative: 98%
% decisions issued within applicable deadline
Share of cases where the written care decision notice is issued within the applicable deadline type (5 / 10 / 25 working days), accounting for any valid pause.
Illustrative: 95%
Count / value of €70-per-week penalty payments
Number of cases triggering the statutory penalty for a missed decision deadline, and the total value paid, per reporting period.
Illustrative: tracked, target trend downward
Repeat-request rate
Share of cases requiring more than one missing-information request before the order information is judged complete.
Illustrative: below 10%
Targets shown are illustrative thresholds for demonstration purposes only and have not been validated against NordCare's actual operating performance or agreed management targets.
4. Control Ownership
Case Handler (Sachspezialist für Pflege): owns case-level control execution, including completeness checks, deadline monitoring, and handover discipline for assigned cases.
Zero-Gap Agent: executes the automated completeness check and surfaces deadline-risk flags for Case Handler and Team Lead review.
Decision Intelligence Agent: executes the Gutachten plausibility check and drafts the benefit-entitlement determination for Case Handler review.
Team Lead: owns operational escalation handling and day-to-day performance monitoring across a team of cases.
Process Owner: owns the overall control framework, KPI reporting, penalty tracking, and approval of any change to the process or its controls.
5. Issue & Improvement Management
Identify the issue through KPI monitoring, escalation records, penalty triggers, or direct case-handler feedback.
Log the issue with the affected case(s), process stage, and observed impact.
Conduct root-cause analysis, distinguishing one-off case errors from systemic process, data, or agent-performance causes.
Define and assign a corrective action, with an owner and target completion date.
Implement the corrective action and verify its effect against the relevant KPI over the following reporting period.
Record the resolved issue and its root cause in the governance log for trend analysis.
6. Records & Evidence
Case-level logs of completeness checks, deadline clock events, handovers, and objection outcomes.
Monthly KPI reporting pack, including penalty payment tracking.
Escalation records with trigger, action taken, and owner.
Issue and improvement log with root causes and corrective actions.
7. Policy Governance
This policy, and the KPI targets and control ownership it describes, are illustrative and fictitious, prepared for internal demonstration purposes as part of a consulting engagement. They do not represent an approved operational policy and must be reviewed and approved by a designated Process Owner, with input from Legal and Compliance, before any operational use.

json.text:
Zero Gap Agent — Completeness Check Operating Procedure
How the Zero Gap Agent checks initial long-term care applications for missing information before the formal medical assessment — NordCare Pflegekasse, Long-Term Care Claims Operations
1. Purpose
This procedure defines how the Zero Gap Agent scans initial applications for long-term care benefits (Antrag auf Leistungen der Pflegeversicherung, object “Care Application”) and flags missing legal or personal parameters before the formal medical assessment is scheduled. The agent does not deny an application because details are missing. Its role is to halt the pipeline and flag the file for a quick data-gathering workflow, so that the strict 25-working-day window can be met.
2. Scope
Applies to initial Pflegeversicherung (long-term care insurance) benefit application intake only.
Completeness of Objection cases is out of scope for this demo.
The agent performs the completeness check on the Document object, but ingests the case-level timestamp (the initial “formless Antrag” date) to calculate SLA risk and track the days remaining on the statutory clock.
Primary inputs: official multi-page PDF/scanned application forms, formal representation authorizations (Vollmacht), and supplementary clinical logs.
3. Mandatory Fields & Validation Rules
The agent verifies the presence of the following critical sections of the application form under German social security standards.
Form section
Required fields
Rule / result if not met
1. Applicant Data
Full name, date of birth, insurance number (Versichertennummer), current address.
Hard failure if the insurance number is missing or mismatched, or if basic identity does not match. This prevents eligibility routing.
2. Legal Representation
Representative name and contact; legal guardian (Betreuer) checkbox; authorized representative / proxy (Bevollmächtigter) checkbox.
Conditional: if “yes” is checked, a matching power of attorney or court decree (Vorsorgevollmacht / Betreuungsausweis) must be attached.
3. Type of Benefit
At least one selected: care allowance (Pflegegeld), non-cash care benefits (Pflegesachleistung), combination benefit (Kombinationsleistung), fully inpatient care (Vollstationäre Pflege).
No selection: soft warning for the 3-day MD commissioning deadline; hard failure (drafted outreach letter) for the final 25-day decision phase.
4. Medical Contacts
Name and address of the general practitioner (Hausarzt); treaters/specialists optional but strongly preferred.
If blank, flagged as a soft warning, not a hard failure. The insurer needs these contacts to request medical history before the assessment.
5. Care Providers
Contact details of the family caregiver, or of the outpatient care service (Ambulanter Pflegedienst).
Mandatory only if Pflegegeld, Pflegesachleistung or Kombinationsleistung is selected.
6. Execution
Date, location, and signature (wet or digital).
Hard failure if unsigned. Unsigned forms cannot legally initiate processing.
7. SLA Triggers
Accelerated statutory deadline triggers, e.g. hospitalization, inpatient rehab, family care leave (checkboxes or keywords).
If detected, the agent overrides the standard 25-day clock and tags the case “Urgent SLA: 5-Day/10-Day”.
8. Civil Servant (Beamter)
Civil service subsidy office (Beihilfestelle) checkbox.
For civil servant applications, the checkbox must be verified so that cost-splitting is configured correctly.
Happy-path checks are hardcoded in the agent prompt. Edge cases (missing documents, civil service, power-of-attorney mismatch, benefit-type conditional logic) are pulled live from ARIS via MCP. Completeness rules are maintained as one SOP-style policy document per benefit type (e.g. “Completeness Policy: Pflegegeld v1.2”), written in insurer voice, listing required fields, legal basis and escalation rule, and stored as an ARIS-attached satellite document.
4. Completeness Check Procedure
The check fires on the document ingestion event.
The agent timestamps the case from first applicant contact (the “formless Antrag” date), separately from when it runs the completeness check. The 25-working-day statutory clock starts at first contact, independent of when the document arrives.
The agent links the document to the case. It matches by insurance number (Versichertennummer) if present; otherwise it uses a probabilistic match on name + date of birth + date of application. Every non-exact match is flagged “assumed link — no primary key”.
The agent scans for accelerated statutory deadline triggers (Section 3, row 7). If detected, it overrides the standard 25-day clock and tags the case “Urgent SLA: 5-Day/10-Day”.
The agent validates each form section against Section 3, including the Beihilfestelle check for civil servant applications, and records every hard failure and soft warning.
If a care diary (Pflegetagebuch) or hospital discharge report (Entlassungsbericht) is present, the agent catalogs it as a verified attachment and ties it to the case file for the medical appraiser — only if an exact primary key match exists. If the case link is an “assumed link” (probabilistic match), these medical documents are strictly quarantined for human verification.
The agent calculates SLA risk and the days remaining on the statutory clock from the case-level timestamp.
The agent returns a binary result — “Ready for Assessment” or “Missing Information” — with a structured list of the specific missing or failed fields.
5. Missing-Information Handling
Escalation branch: If information is missing, the agent may escalate to the case manager with a plain-language summary of the gap.
Outreach branch: Alternatively, the agent drafts an outreach letter to the applicant requesting the missing item(s).
All drafted outreach letters and case manager escalations are placed in the human-in-the-loop queue, each visibly tagged with a dynamic countdown timer (“Days to SLA Breach”), so that caseworkers prioritize requests that pause the penalty clock.
No outbound communication (letter or escalation) leaves the system without human review and sign-off. There is no auto-send under any condition.
All agent outputs (flags, notifications, drafted letters) are issued in German.
6. Roles
Zero Gap Agent: runs the completeness check on ingested documents, links documents to cases, detects SLA triggers, returns the binary result, and drafts outreach letters or escalations for human review.
Caseworker: reviews and signs off drafted letters and escalations in the human-in-the-loop queue, prioritizing by the “Days to SLA Breach” countdown.
Case Manager: receives agent escalations with a plain-language summary of the gap.
Human verifier: verifies care diaries and discharge reports quarantined because of an assumed case link.
Medical appraiser: receives the verified attachments tied to the case file.
7. Escalation
When information is missing, the agent may escalate to the case manager with a plain-language summary of the gap, as an alternative to drafting an outreach letter. Escalations follow the same rules as letters: they are placed in the human-in-the-loop queue with the “Days to SLA Breach” countdown and require human review and sign-off before leaving the system. Medical documents linked through an “assumed link” are quarantined for human verification rather than cataloged.
8. Agent Output & Closure Criteria
Binary result recorded: “Ready for Assessment” or “Missing Information”.
Structured list of the specific missing or failed fields.
Case timestamp from first applicant contact and days remaining on the statutory clock.
Deadline tag: standard 25-day clock, or “Urgent SLA: 5-Day/10-Day”.
Case-link status: exact match on insurance number, or “assumed link — no primary key”.
Attachment status: care diary / discharge report cataloged as verified, or quarantined for human verification.
Every outbound letter or escalation carries human sign-off before it leaves the system.
9. Legal & Local Rules Applied
“Formless Antrag” precedent: In Germany, a care application is legally valid from the day a single sentence requesting care is received, even by phone or email.
Statutory clocks: 25-working-day statutory window, starting at first applicant contact; 3-day deadline for commissioning the Medical Service (MD).
Accelerated deadlines: hospitalization, inpatient rehab or family care leave triggers override the standard 25-day clock with a 5-day or 10-day deadline.
Validity of the application: unsigned forms cannot legally initiate processing; without a selected benefit type, the application cannot be legally prioritized or calculated.
Civil servants: civil servant (Beamter) applications require the Beihilfestelle checkbox for correct cost-splitting.
10. Open Points
Output language: German only, or also English, is marked TBD. The background specification describes a bilingual German/English notification payload.
Type of Benefit: the requirements set a soft warning for the 3-day deadline and a hard failure for the 25-day phase; the background specification describes it as a hard failure. This procedure follows the requirements.
Escalation vs. outreach: the criteria for choosing escalation versus outreach are not specified.
Human verifier: the role that performs human verification of quarantined medical documents is not specified.

drafts.outreach_letter:
Dear Markus Hoffmann,

Regarding the application for long-term care benefits for Ingrid Hoffmann: to process the application we require the following documents. Each of them is mandatory:

1. Medical reports and diagnosis from all treating doctors
2. Hospital discharge report (Entlassungsbericht)
3. Copy of the applicant’s identity card
4. Bank details and last three bank statements
5. Care provider contract

Please send all documents within 7 days.

Kind regards
Your Care Insurance Fund
